title: There is no "save as" dialogua when using Zoomit screen recording
summary: ZoomIt recording ends with no Save As dialog or file; current code has a silent zero-frame return path that matches that user experience.
next_action: Keep the lightweight design candidate deferred and use the maintainer reproduction plan to confirm whether the session is ending with zero captured frames.

confidence.rationale: The code already contains a silent no-video-frames branch that directly explains the missing Save As dialog, even though the upstream reason for zero frames may vary by environment.

judgment.rationale: There is a concrete repo-side improvement path in ZoomIt’s recording workflow, even before the exact capture-environment cause is known.
evidence: The reporter sees the yellow recording frame appear, then disappear on the second Ctrl+5 press, with no Save As dialog and no file saved.
In src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp, the MP4 path deletes the temporary file and returns silently when HasCapturedVideoFrames() is false after recording completes.
ZoomIt already has a WM_USER_RECORDING_NO_FRAMES warning path, but the explicit zero-frame early return bypasses that user-facing message.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat the silent zero-frame branch as the current fix target and reproduce the issue on a constrained environment before expanding to a deeper capture-pipeline design.

fix_assessment.rationale: A focused code change can eliminate the silent-failure behavior by routing zero-frame exits through an explicit warning/logging path.

issue_context.summary: The core user-visible failure is not just that recording does not save; it is that ZoomIt provides no Save As dialog and no explanation after recording is stopped.
known_information: The report is against PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store.
Ctrl+5 starts recording and shows the yellow frame; pressing Ctrl+5 again ends that visual state, but no Save As dialog appears and no MP4 is found.
The reporter notes this is on a company PC and wonders whether policy may be involved.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP was attached.
inferences: The capture session may be ending before the first frame arrives, which would bypass the save dialog even though the UI briefly showed a recording border.
Corporate graphics-capture policy or environment differences could be the upstream trigger, but the silent exit is still a repo-local UX/diagnostic gap.
issue_context.analysis: The current code already contains a branch that silently deletes the temp recording and returns when zero frames were captured. That makes this a useful lightweight design candidate even before the exact environment cause is confirmed.
initial_investigation: ZoomIt recording/save flow is implemented in src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomIt/Zoomit.cpp and VideoRecordingSession.cpp.
The MP4 and GIF paths both contain explicit “no frames captured” early returns before the Save As dialog.
Earlier ZoomIt work in PR #49553 focused on trim/save reliability, but this thread’s symptom happens even earlier in the flow.

actions.label: Approve zero-frame recording design
actions.note: Deferred from full design in this bounded batch; the artifact keeps a lightweight fix path ready.

actions.label: Reproduce missing Save As path
actions.note: The remaining uncertainty is environment-specific and maintainer-side; the current code already suggests a zero-frame recording branch.

reproduce.title: Exercise ZoomIt recording until the save workflow should appear
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2362 or newer with ZoomIt screen recording enabled
prerequisites: Windows desktop session with ZoomIt enabled
A display environment as close as possible to the reporter, ideally including any corporate policy constraints if reproducible
setup: Configure Ctrl+5 screen recording with default MP4 output.
If possible, test both a normal desktop and an environment with restricted capture or graphics virtualization.
steps: Press Ctrl+5 to start screen recording and verify the yellow frame appears.
Press Ctrl+5 again to stop recording after a short capture interval.
Observe whether Save As appears, whether a warning is shown, and whether any recording file is created.
reproduce.expected_result: Successful recordings should open the Save As / trim workflow. If no frames were captured, ZoomIt should show a clear warning instead of silently doing nothing.

proposed_fixes.title: Surface zero-frame recording failures instead of silently returning
proposed_fixes.root_cause: ZoomIt’s post-recording flow currently deletes the temporary recording and returns without any Save As dialog or warning when the session ends before a video frame is captured. That produces exactly the “yellow frame disappears, nothing saved, no dialog” experience reported here.
plan: Extract the zero-frame cleanup into a shared helper used by both GIF and MP4 recording paths.
On zero-frame exit, post the existing WM_USER_RECORDING_NO_FRAMES warning or a more specific message before returning so the user learns why Save As never opened.
Log whether the session ended due to no captured frames, capture-start failure, or a blocked graphics-capture environment, and keep the normal Save As path unchanged for successful recordings.
verification: Reproduce a zero-frame recording environment and verify ZoomIt shows an explanatory warning instead of silently disappearing.
Verify successful recordings still reach the Save As / trim workflow and save normally.

confidence.rationale: The silent return path is directly present in current code and closely matches the symptom, although the reason no frames were captured may still be environmental.

deferred_reason: The batch used its single full-design slot on Issue 50239; this issue keeps lightweight fix coverage only.
